intro.title: What does Exyconn build for restaurants?
intro.definition: is a set of agents that take bookings, answer the phone, take orders and keep track of stock and costs, so the floor and kitchen team spend service on guests and food rather than on calls and spreadsheets. Exyconn designs, builds and runs these agents on top of your POS, kitchen display and delivery-app accounts. Every order still lands as a normal KOT in the kitchen.

benefits.title: Why restaurants are doing this now

items.text: The phone rings hardest at 8pm, when nobody on the floor can step away to answer it.
Orders taken on your own phone line or WhatsApp carry no aggregator commission.
Ingredient prices move week to week, and margins on a dish can disappear without anyone noticing.
Kitchen and floor staff turn over often, so process has to live somewhere other than people's heads.
Diners check ratings on Google and Zomato before they book, and they read the replies too.

props.label: The reality
props.title: Where a restaurant's hours actually go
props.lede: Ask a restaurant manager what goes wrong on a busy night and the answer is rarely the food.

items.title: Calls that ring out during service
items.text: Bookings and takeaway orders come by phone at peak hours. When nobody can answer, the guest calls the next place on the list.

items.title: No-shows and a messy waitlist
items.text: A table held for a party that never turns up is a table lost on the best night of the week. Walk-ins meanwhile wait at the door with a name scribbled on paper.

items.title: A wall of delivery tablets
items.text: Swiggy, Zomato and your own website each ping on their own device. Orders get accepted late, items are marked out of stock in one app and not the others.

items.title: Wastage nobody measures
items.text: Prep is done by habit, closing stock is counted by eye and spoilage goes in the bin unrecorded. The gap shows up only when the month's purchase bills arrive.

items.title: Feedback in too many places
items.text: A cold biryani complaint on a delivery app, a five-star note on Google and a grumble to the server never meet, so the kitchen hears about problems late.

items.title: Food cost worked out once a month
items.text: Recipe costing sits in a spreadsheet nobody updates. When onion or paneer prices jump, nobody knows which dishes stopped making money.

offerings.title: Six jobs AI takes off the floor and the pass

items.title: Reservations and the waitlist
items.text: Books tables from WhatsApp, the website and Google against your floor plan, confirms the day before to cut no-shows, and texts walk-ins when their table is ready.

items.title: Phone and WhatsApp orders by voice
items.text: A voice agent answers the restaurant line, takes takeaway and delivery orders item by item with modifiers, reads back the total and sends a KOT straight to the POS.

items.title: Delivery-app orders in one queue
items.text: Pulls orders from aggregators and your own site into one view, keeps item availability in step across every app and warns the manager when an order is waiting too long to be accepted.

items.title: Inventory and wastage
items.text: Deducts ingredients from stock as dishes sell using your recipes in the POS, takes closing counts and spoilage by voice or photo from the kitchen, and drafts purchase orders for the manager to approve.

items.title: Reviews and guest feedback
items.text: Collects reviews from Google and the delivery apps, drafts replies for a manager to approve, and sends the kitchen a short note when the same dish keeps getting the same complaint.

items.title: Sales and food-cost reports
items.text: Builds the end-of-day report from the POS: covers, average bill, channel mix and theoretical versus actual food cost, with the dishes whose margin slipped this week at the top.

moments.title: Last night's stock, counted
moments.text: The sous chef walks the cold room and reads out closing counts. The agent compares them with what the POS says was used, flags extra paneer wastage and drafts the vegetable order.

moments.title: Lunch orders on one screen

moments.title: Tonight's bookings, reconfirmed
moments.text: Every booking for tonight gets a WhatsApp reminder. Two parties cancel, their tables go back on sale and a waitlisted family of five is offered one.

moments.title: The phone picks up on the first ring
moments.text: Peak service, and the takeaway line is ringing. The voice agent takes an order for three curries, rotis and a raita, confirms the pickup time and sends the KOT to the kitchen.

moments.title: A complaint reaches the kitchen
moments.text: A delivery review says the dal makhani arrived lukewarm. The manager approves an apology, and the head chef gets a note that it's the third packaging complaint this week.

moments.title: Food cost, the same night
moments.text: The owner gets covers, average bill, delivery versus dine-in and the day's food cost, with a line pointing out that the paneer dishes lost margin after this week's price rise.

items.question: Will the AI replace my captains or my host?
items.answer: No. It answers the phone and the messages your team can't get to during service, and keeps the paperwork moving. Greeting guests, running tables and handling a complaint at the table stay with your people.

items.question: Can a voice agent really take a phone order correctly?
items.answer: It takes the order from your live POS menu, asks about portions and modifiers, reads the order and total back and only sends the KOT once the caller confirms. If a caller asks for something off-menu or gets frustrated, the call is passed to a staff member.

items.question: Which POS and delivery apps does it work with?
items.answer: Any POS with an API or a dependable export, and delivery orders through whatever integration your POS already has with the aggregators. We confirm what your setup can read and write in the first week, before anything goes live.

items.question: Does it handle Hindi and regional languages on calls?
items.answer: Yes. The voice and chat agents work in English, Hindi and other Indian languages, and can switch mid-conversation when a caller does.

items.question: What about allergies and food safety?
items.answer: The agent records allergies and dietary needs on the booking and the KOT, and answers ingredient questions only from the recipes you've approved. If it isn't sure, it says so and passes the question to the kitchen. Your FSSAI licence and food safety duties stay with your team.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: It depends on the number of outlets, phone lines and systems. Most restaurants start with reservations or phone ordering at one outlet; tell us about yours and we'll send a fixed quote for the first phase.
